description: Two integer-allocation routines are stubbed out of a Python telemetry toolkit and must be rebuilt in exact rational arithmetic: Hamilton apportionment whose three-key remainder/quota/index tie-break decides the last unit, and a minimum-penalty placement over arbitrary per-bucket penalty rows where the marginal-cost greedy exchange argument is only valid under discrete convexity, so non-convex rows force a dynamic program whose reconstruction must run forward to yield the lexicographically smallest optimum.
